g.text: Normalization existence: the Gauss closure and its return
Rank-one V; algebraically closed K; F = K(T); finite separable L/F. Proof locators: I.8–I.9.
Original valued field
U = V[T] at the Gauss prime mV[T]
W = integral closure of U in L
I.3, I.7: W ⊗ᵤ U′ = W′; U → U′ faithfully flat
Completed constants; exact normal model
B = integral closure of A in L ⊗ꜰ Frac(A)
I.8: B finite normal over A; U′ = R at q; W′ = (B°) at q
dense
extension
The finite-rank mechanism (I.9)
Separating coordinates: B finite over K̂⟨w⟩, and B̃ finite separating over k[w].
For d ≥ 1 (d = 0 is immediate): polynomial approximation gives D = K̂[w][η], rank b.
Vν = {f ∈ D : pole order at infinity ≤ ν}
Choose fⱼ of norm 1 in ker(ev z₁,…,ev zⱼ₋₁), with |fⱼ(zⱼ)| = 1.
The evaluation matrix is triangular: |Σ aⱼ fⱼ| = max |aⱼ|.
Thus f̃ⱼ are independent: dim K̂ Vν ≤ dim k B̃(ν).
(b/d!) νᵈ + O(νᵈ⁻¹) ≤ (b̃/d!) νᵈ + O(νᵈ⁻¹)
Together with b̃ ≤ b, this yields b̃ = b. Total-degree count: binomial(n+d,d).
Return to the original coefficient ring; then normalization
Trace coordinates + bounded saturated-module division: B° finite over V̂⟨w⟩.
Q = R[h₁,…,hₘ] is finite over R and contains V̂⟨w⟩ by monic bounded-power reduction.
Therefore B° finite over R → W′ finite over U′ → W finite over U.
Exact ring maps are inclusions or the indicated faithfully flat tensor comparison. B° denotes power-bounded elements;
B̃ denotes B° modulo topologically nilpotent elements. This is a proof schematic, not a spatial or numerical model.
